subject: opinions on pruning Boost in Stan

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: opinions on pruning Boost in Stan
parts:
For the sake of maintenance, I would rather not prune. Right now, it's really easy to drop a new Boost into Stan. We just unpack it into lib/, delete the old folder, update the make target. If someone could script something really robust that would work, then that's fine too -- I'd need the script in hand to be convinced.

And disk space is cheap.


On Thu, May 30, 2013 at 9:13 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
Disk space is cheap these days, so I'd say it is worth it. Besides, at some point we should prune down boost from the main Stan repository.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: opinions on pruning Boost in Stan
parts:
There is a script in TO-DO.txt

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ grep -F "bcp" TO-DO.txt
  find ${STAN_HOME}/src/ -name \*\.\[ch]pp -exec bcp --scan --boost=${STAN_HOME}/lib/boost_1.52.0 '{}' /tmp/boost_1.52.0/ \; &> /tmp/boost_1.52.0/bcp.log

although I guess you would need to change to 1.53.0 now. And you need to build or otherwise have the bcp executable.

Ben
